title: Export every customer with cursor pagination
brief:
Write `async function listAllCustomerIds(api)` that returns the ids of **all** customers, in API order, by walking `GET /v1/customers` page by page.

- Request the largest page the API allows (`limit=100`) to minimise calls.
- Follow `has_more` / `starting_after` until done.
- Handle 429 and transient 5xx exactly as the docs describe.
- If a request still fails after 5 attempts, **throw** an `Error`.
docs:
## Customers API (fake)

### GET /v1/customers

Query parameters:

| name | type | notes |
|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | 1–100, default 10. The server may cap it lower. |
| `starting_after` | string | A customer id. Returns objects strictly after it. |

Response 200:

```json
{ "object": "list", "data": [{ "id": "cus_001", "email": "user1@example.com" }], "has_more": true }
```

To get the next page, pass `starting_after` = the id of the **last** object in the current `data`. Stop when `has_more` is `false`. An unknown cursor returns 400.

### Conventions (all endpoints)

- `api.request(method, path, { query, body, headers })` resolves to `{ status, headers, body }`. Response header names are **lowercase**.
- Errors have the body `{ error: { type, message, code? } }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: the response has a `retry-after` header in **seconds** (string). Wait exactly that long (`await api.sleep(seconds * 1000)`) and retry the same request.
- **500 / 503**: transient. Retry with exponential backoff: wait **200 ms** after the 1st failure, 400 ms after the 2nd, 800 ms, 1600 ms ... (`200 * 2^(attempt-1)`).
- Make **at most 5 attempts** per request (429s and 5xx both count). If the 5th attempt still fails, give up (see the task for what to return/throw).
- Other 4xx errors are permanent: never retry them.
- `api.sleep(ms)` advances a virtual clock instantly; `api.now()` returns the virtual time in ms. Never use `setTimeout`.

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 3 }); const r = await listAllCustomerIds(api); return { r, calls: api.calls.length }; })()

tests.name: follows has_more / starting_after
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 7, maxLimit: 3 }); const r = await listAllCustomerIds(api); return { count: r.length, last: r[6], calls: api.calls.length, cursors: api.calls.map((c) => c.query.starting_after || null) }; })()

tests.name: empty list
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 0 }); const r = await listAllCustomerIds(api); return { r, calls: api.calls.length }; })()

tests.name: requests limit=100
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 2 }); await listAllCustomerIds(api); return Number(api.calls[0].query.limit); })()

tests.name: 429 waits Retry-After seconds
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 4, maxLimit: 2, rateLimitOn: [2], retryAfter: 3 }); const r = await listAllCustomerIds(api); return { count: r.length, sleeps: api.sleeps, calls: api.calls.length }; })()

tests.name: transient 503 retried with backoff
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 3, failOn: [1, 2] }); const r = await listAllCustomerIds(api); return { count: r.length, sleeps: api.sleeps }; })()

tests.name: gives up after 5 attempts
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ total: 3, failFrom: 1 }); try { await listAllCustomerIds(api); return { threw: false, calls: api.calls.length }; } catch (e) { return { threw: true, calls: api.calls.length }; } })()

hints: Write one helper `send(api, method, path, opts)` that owns retries; keep pagination logic separate.
The cursor is the id of the last item of the page you just received, not a page number.
Read the header as `res.headers["retry-after"]`; it is in seconds, sleep takes milliseconds.
keyPoints: Loop terminates on has_more === false (and defensively on an empty page)
Cursor taken from the last element of data; limit maximised
Retry logic isolated in a reusable helper; 429 honours Retry-After, 5xx uses exponential backoff
Bounded attempts; failure surfaces as a thrown error instead of a partial silent result

title: Create charges idempotently with safe retries
brief:
Write `async function createCharges(api, orders)`. Each order is `{ orderId, amount, currency, source }`. Process orders **sequentially** and return one result per order, in order:

- success: `{ orderId, chargeId }`
- permanent API error (4xx other than 429): `{ orderId, error: <error.code> }` (do not retry)
- still 429/5xx after 5 attempts: `{ orderId, error: "max_retries" }`

Every POST must carry the header `Idempotency-Key: charge-<orderId>`, and retries of the same order must reuse the same key, so a lost response never causes a double charge. One failed order must not stop the others.
docs:
## Charges API (fake)

### POST /v1/charges

Headers: `Idempotency-Key` (**required**, string up to 255 chars).

Body: `{ amount: integer (minor units), currency: string, source: string }`

Response 200: `{ id: "ch_1", amount, currency, status: "succeeded" }`

Errors:

| status | error.code | meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `missing_idempotency_key` | no key sent |
| 400 | `idempotency_key_reused` | key already used with **different** parameters |
| 402 | `card_declined` | `source` is `tok_declined` |

**Idempotency:** the first request with a given key is executed and its response (success *or* error) is stored for 24 h. Any later request with the same key and same parameters returns the stored response (with header `idempotent-replayed: true`) and does not create another charge. Note that a 5xx may be returned **after** the charge was created (the response was lost in transit); retrying with the same key is the safe way to find out what happened.

### Conventions (all endpoints)

- `api.request(method, path, { query, body, headers })` resolves to `{ status, headers, body }`. Response header names are **lowercase**.
- Errors have the body `{ error: { type, message, code? } }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: the response has a `retry-after` header in **seconds** (string). Wait exactly that long (`await api.sleep(seconds * 1000)`) and retry the same request.
- **500 / 503**: transient. Retry with exponential backoff: wait **200 ms** after the 1st failure, 400 ms after the 2nd, 800 ms, 1600 ms ... (`200 * 2^(attempt-1)`).
- Make **at most 5 attempts** per request (429s and 5xx both count). If the 5th attempt still fails, give up (see the task for what to return/throw).
- Other 4xx errors are permanent: never retry them.
- `api.sleep(ms)` advances a virtual clock instantly; `api.now()` returns the virtual time in ms. Never use `setTimeout`.

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi(); const r = await createCharges(api, [{ orderId: "A", amount: 500, currency: "usd", source: "tok_visa" }, { orderId: "B", amount: 900, currency: "usd", source: "tok_visa" }]); return { r, calls: api.calls.length }; })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi(); await createCharges(api, [{ orderId: "A", amount: 500, currency: "usd", source: "tok_visa" }]); const h = api.calls[0].headers; const k = Object.keys(h).find((x) => x.toLowerCase() === "idempotency-key"); return h[k]; })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ rateLimitOn: [1], retryAfter: 2 }); const r = await createCharges(api, [{ orderId: "A", amount: 500, currency: "usd", source: "tok_visa" }]); return { r, sleeps: api.sleeps }; })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ failFrom: 1 }); const r = await createCharges(api, [{ orderId: "A", amount: 500, currency: "usd", source: "tok_visa" }]); return { r, calls: api.calls.length, sleeps: api.sleeps }; })()

hints: Derive the key from the order (charge-<orderId>), compute it once per order, outside the retry loop.
A 503 does not mean the charge failed. The retry with the same key returns the stored result.
Classify each final response: 200, retryable exhausted, or permanent 4xx with error.code.
keyPoints: Idempotency key is deterministic per logical operation and identical across retries
Only 429/5xx retried; 402/400 surfaced immediately with the API's error code
Bounded retries with exponential backoff; Retry-After respected
Per-order failure isolation: results array always has one entry per order
Understands that 5xx is ambiguous (operation may have committed)

title: Bulk-update metadata under a rate limit
brief:
Write `async function bulkUpdateMetadata(api, ids, metadata)` that sets `metadata` on every customer in `ids` via `POST /v1/customers/:id`, sequentially, in the given order.

Return `{ updated: [ids...], notFound: [ids...], failed: [ids...] }` (each in input order): `notFound` for 404s, `failed` for anything that still fails after 5 attempts. The account has a tight rate limit; you must wait exactly the advertised `Retry-After` rather than hammering the API.
docs:
## Customers API (fake)

### POST /v1/customers/:id

Body: `{ metadata: { [key]: string } }`. Keys are **merged** into the existing metadata.

Response 200: the updated customer `{ id, metadata }`. 404 `resource_missing` if the customer does not exist (ids starting with `cus_missing` never exist).

### Rate limiting

Requests are limited by a token bucket: capacity `burst` tokens, refilled continuously at `ratePerSec` tokens per second (virtual clock). Each request costs one token. When the bucket is empty the API answers **429** with `retry-after` = the whole number of seconds until a token is available. Requests that get a 429 consume nothing.

### Conventions (all endpoints)

- `api.request(method, path, { query, body, headers })` resolves to `{ status, headers, body }`. Response header names are **lowercase**.
- Errors have the body `{ error: { type, message, code? } }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: the response has a `retry-after` header in **seconds** (string). Wait exactly that long (`await api.sleep(seconds * 1000)`) and retry the same request.
- **500 / 503**: transient. Retry with exponential backoff: wait **200 ms** after the 1st failure, 400 ms after the 2nd, 800 ms, 1600 ms ... (`200 * 2^(attempt-1)`).
- Make **at most 5 attempts** per request (429s and 5xx both count). If the 5th attempt still fails, give up (see the task for what to return/throw).
- Other 4xx errors are permanent: never retry them.
- `api.sleep(ms)` advances a virtual clock instantly; `api.now()` returns the virtual time in ms. Never use `setTimeout`.

tests.name: updates and merges metadata
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi(); const r = await bulkUpdateMetadata(api, ["cus_1", "cus_2"], { tier: "gold" }); return { r, meta: api.state.customers.cus_1.metadata, calls: api.calls.length }; })()

tests.name: 404s reported, not retried

tests.name: never two 429s in a row when waiting correctly
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ burst: 1, ratePerSec: 0.5 }); await bulkUpdateMetadata(api, ["c1", "c2", "c3"], { a: "1" }); const s = api.calls.map((c) => c.status); let streak = 0, max = 0; for (const x of s) { streak = x === 429 ? streak + 1 : 0; max = Math.max(max, streak); } return { max, sleeps: api.sleeps }; })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ failOn: [2] }); const r = await bulkUpdateMetadata(api, ["c1", "c2"], { a: "1" }); return { r, sleeps: api.sleeps }; })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ failOn: [2, 3, 4, 5, 6] }); const r = await bulkUpdateMetadata(api, ["c1", "c2", "c3"], { a: "1" }); return { r, calls: api.calls.length }; })()

404 is permanent; record it and move on.
Counting attempts per id (not globally) keeps one bad id from starving the rest.
keyPoints: Uses Retry-After instead of a fixed or exponential guess for 429
Per-item outcome classification (updated / notFound / failed)
Bounded retries per item; a single failure does not abort the batch
Sequential processing (no unbounded parallelism against a rate-limited API)

title: Verify webhook signatures and process events once
brief:
Write `async function handleWebhooks(api, deliveries, secret)`. Each delivery is `{ payload, header }` where `payload` is the raw JSON string body and `header` is the `Signature` header value (possibly missing). Return an array with one status string per delivery, in order:

1. `"malformed"`: header missing/unparseable, or no `t`, or no `v1`.
2. `"invalid_signature"`: no `v1` matches the expected signature.
3. `"stale"`: signature valid but timestamp more than 300 s away from `api.now()`.
4. `"duplicate"`: an event with the same `id` was already processed in this call.
5. `"processed"`: otherwise. For these (and only these), call `POST /v1/fulfillments` with `{ event_id, type }` (with the standard retry policy).

Check in that order. Verify the signature against the **raw** payload string, never a re-serialised object.
docs:
## Webhook signatures (fake)

Each delivery has a header:

```
Signature: t=1700000000,v1=5f2b1c0a,v1=9a8b7c6d
```

- Comma-separated `key=value` pairs. `t` is the Unix timestamp in **seconds** at signing time. There may be **several** `v1` entries (during secret rotation); the delivery is authentic if **any** of them matches. Unknown keys must be ignored.
- Expected signature: `api.hash(secret + "." + t + "." + payload)` where `t` is the exact string from the header and `payload` the raw body. `api.hash` returns 8 lowercase hex chars (FNV-1a 32-bit; a stand-in for HMAC-SHA256).
- Tolerance: reject if `|api.now()/1000 - t| > 300`.
- Payload is JSON: `{ id: "evt_...", type: "...", data: {...} }`.
- Test helper (also available to you): `signHeader(api, secret, t, payload)` returns `"t=<t>,v1=<sig>"`.

### POST /v1/fulfillments

Body `{ event_id, type }` → 200 `{ ok: true }`.

### Conventions (all endpoints)

- `api.request(method, path, { query, body, headers })` resolves to `{ status, headers, body }`. Response header names are **lowercase**.
- Errors have the body `{ error: { type, message, code? } }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: the response has a `retry-after` header in **seconds** (string). Wait exactly that long (`await api.sleep(seconds * 1000)`) and retry the same request.
- **500 / 503**: transient. Retry with exponential backoff: wait **200 ms** after the 1st failure, 400 ms after the 2nd, 800 ms, 1600 ms ... (`200 * 2^(attempt-1)`).
- Make **at most 5 attempts** per request (429s and 5xx both count). If the 5th attempt still fails, give up (see the task for what to return/throw).
- Other 4xx errors are permanent: never retry them.
- `api.sleep(ms)` advances a virtual clock instantly; `api.now()` returns the virtual time in ms. Never use `setTimeout`.

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ startMs: 1700000000000 }); const p = JSON.stringify({ id: "evt_1", type: "charge.succeeded" }); const r = await handleWebhooks(api, [{ payload: p, header: signHeader(api, "whsec_a", 1700000000, p) }], "whsec_a"); return { r, fulfilled: api.state.fulfilled }; })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ startMs: 1700000000000 }); const mk = (id, t) => { const p = JSON.stringify({ id, type: "x" }); return { payload: p, header: signHeader(api, "s", t, p) }; }; return await handleWebhooks(api, [mk("e1", 1700000000 - 300), mk("e2", 1700000000 - 301), mk("e3", 1700000000 + 200), mk("e4", 1700000000 + 400)], "s"); })()

tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ startMs: 1700000000000 }); const p = JSON.stringify({ id: "evt_9", type: "invoice.paid" }); const good = api.hash("s_new." + 1700000000 + "." + p); const h = "t=1700000000,v0=zzz,v1=00000000,v1=" + good; return await handleWebhooks(api, [{ payload: p, header: h }], "s_new"); })()

tests.name: duplicate events processed once
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ startMs: 1700000000000 }); const p = JSON.stringify({ id: "evt_1", type: "charge.succeeded" }); const d = { payload: p, header: signHeader(api, "s", 1700000000, p) }; const r = await handleWebhooks(api, [d, d], "s"); return { r, fulfilled: api.state.fulfilled }; })()

tests.name: fulfillment call retried on 503
tests.call: (async () => { const api = createApi({ startMs: 1700000000000, failOn: [1] }); const p = JSON.stringify({ id: "evt_1", type: "charge.succeeded" }); const r = await handleWebhooks(api, [{ payload: p, header: signHeader(api, "s", 1700000000, p) }], "s"); return { r, fulfilled: api.state.fulfilled, sleeps: api.sleeps }; })()

hints: Parse the header into { t, v1: [] } by splitting on commas and then on the first '='.
Compute the expected signature from the raw payload string and the header's t string; compare against every v1.
Check signature before freshness, and dedupe by event id only after the event is authentic.
keyPoints: Signature computed over the raw body (no JSON round-trip)
Supports multiple v1 signatures; ignores unknown keys
Timestamp tolerance check prevents replay of old deliveries
Constant-time comparison mentioned or used
Idempotent processing: duplicate event ids have no side effects

title: Reconcile payouts against balance transactions
brief:
Finance wants to know which payouts don't add up. Write `async function reconcilePayouts(api)` that:

1. Lists **all** payouts (paginated).
2. For each payout with `status === "paid"` (skip all others; do not fetch their transactions), lists **all** of its balance transactions (paginated) and sums `amount - fee`.
3. Returns the mismatches, in payout list order: `[{ payout, expected, actual, diff }]` where `expected` = payout.amount, `actual` = the sum, `diff = actual - expected`. Return `[]` if everything reconciles.

Use `limit=100`, the standard retry policy, and throw if a request fails permanently.
docs:
## Payouts API (fake)

### GET /v1/payouts

Query: `limit` (1–100, may be capped lower by the server), `starting_after`.

`{ object: "list", data: [{ id: "po_1", amount: 9450, currency: "usd", status: "paid" | "pending" | "failed" }], has_more }`

### GET /v1/balance_transactions

Query: `payout` (**required**, a payout id), `limit`, `starting_after`.

`{ object: "list", data: [{ id: "txn_1_1", amount: 10000, fee: 320, type: "charge" | "refund" | "adjustment" }], has_more }`

Amounts are integers in minor units. Refunds have negative `amount` (and usually `fee: 0`). A payout is correct when `payout.amount === Σ(amount - fee)` over its transactions.

### Conventions (all endpoints)

- `api.request(method, path, { query, body, headers })` resolves to `{ status, headers, body }`. Response header names are **lowercase**.
- Errors have the body `{ error: { type, message, code? } }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: the response has a `retry-after` header in **seconds** (string). Wait exactly that long (`await api.sleep(seconds * 1000)`) and retry the same request.
- **500 / 503**: transient. Retry with exponential backoff: wait **200 ms** after the 1st failure, 400 ms after the 2nd, 800 ms, 1600 ms ... (`200 * 2^(attempt-1)`).
- Make **at most 5 attempts** per request (429s and 5xx both count). If the 5th attempt still fails, give up (see the task for what to return/throw).
- Other 4xx errors are permanent: never retry them.
- `api.sleep(ms)` advances a virtual clock instantly; `api.now()` returns the virtual time in ms. Never use `setTimeout`.

Integer arithmetic on minor units; diff sign is consistent (actual - expected)
No wasted calls for non-paid payouts
Resilient to 429/5xx; permanent failures surface rather than producing a wrong report

title: Poll an async report job with backoff and a deadline
brief:
Write `async function runReport(api, timeoutMs)`:

1. `POST /v1/reports` with body `{ type: "balance" }` to start a job (start time = `api.now()` right before this call).
2. Poll `GET /v1/reports/:id` **immediately**, then after waiting 500 ms, 1000 ms, 2000 ms, 4000 ms, 8000 ms, 8000 ms ... (double, capped at 8000).
3. Return `{ status: "succeeded", url }` (url = `result_url`) or `{ status: "failed", error }` (error = `error_code`) as soon as the job is terminal.
4. Deadline: after a non-terminal poll, if `api.now() - start >= timeoutMs` return `{ status: "timeout" }`. Otherwise never sleep past the deadline: sleep `min(delay, start + timeoutMs - api.now())`.

All requests use the standard retry policy (those sleeps happen too; they are not part of the poll schedule).
docs:

### POST /v1/reports

Body `{ type: "balance" }` → 200 `{ id: "rpt_1", status: "pending" }`.

```json
{ "id": "rpt_1", "status": "pending" | "running" | "succeeded" | "failed",
  "result_url": "https://files.example/rpt_1.csv",   // only when succeeded
  "error_code": "insufficient_data" }                 // only when failed
```

`succeeded` and `failed` are terminal. 404 for unknown ids. Jobs typically finish in seconds to minutes; please back off between polls.

### Conventions (all endpoints)

- `api.request(method, path, { query, body, headers })` resolves to `{ status, headers, body }`. Response header names are **lowercase**.
- Errors have the body `{ error: { type, message, code? } }`.
- **429 Too Many Requests**: the response has a `retry-after` header in **seconds** (string). Wait exactly that long (`await api.sleep(seconds * 1000)`) and retry the same request.
- **500 / 503**: transient. Retry with exponential backoff: wait **200 ms** after the 1st failure, 400 ms after the 2nd, 800 ms, 1600 ms ... (`200 * 2^(attempt-1)`).
- Make **at most 5 attempts** per request (429s and 5xx both count). If the 5th attempt still fails, give up (see the task for what to return/throw).
- Other 4xx errors are permanent: never retry them.
- `api.sleep(ms)` advances a virtual clock instantly; `api.now()` returns the virtual time in ms. Never use `setTimeout`.
